This violates the explicit rule “no private addresses or keys in tracked files or in any message sent.” Concretely, an `unavailable` gate whose reason is `"invalid api key: [REDACTED] matches `_KEY_REASON` and that key value is emitted in the digest message, even though the entry’s own default says never to paste the credential.

chunk_findings.detail: This filter uses `st.items[r["item"]].state != DONE` instead of the file’s own `_is_open`, which excludes both `DONE` and `ABANDONED`. An `ABANDONED` item still has `state != DONE`, so it is included in the operator inbox as “awaiting your spot-check” even though `ABANDONED` is a closed state everywhere else in this file (`collect_phase_close` and `collect_credential` both exclude it). Given an abandoned item with one refuted gate, the digest falsely presents it as work waiting on the operator.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/digest/collect_work.py:collect_gate_spotcheck

chunk_findings.detail: The function unconditionally returns `[]`, so the digest never lists “bugs or completions that need an override the hook forbids to agents” that the intent explicitly requires (fix-Bci-ruff-check..., RM-tool-diet-research, B998bcca9ce style). For any such item, there is no row containing the item or the exact command to answer it; the queue can only name a gap. That leaves a required class of operator-only work out of the read-only inbox.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/digest/collect_work.py:collect_agent_failed

chunk_findings.detail: The `red_main` source row is still classified as `ASK` (the final field in the source tuple), so it will be collected into the folded AW-inbox/`ddflow inbox`. The accepted fold in D-OD-Q4 says that list is only “what only a person can do or decide” (questions, proposed decisions, chore approvals, forced completions/overrides, unavailable-reviewer escalations, contested decisions, partial/forced gates, expired credentials or quota pauses); “main is red” is not one of those inbox items and its command is `ddflow show <task>`, not an exact answer command. Given a failed main CI and no other pending operator asks, the inbox will emit a `red_main` row, which breaks the folded inbox contract. It belongs in the operator work queue (`WORK`), not `ASK`.

chunk_findings.detail: For an OPEN DECIDE doc, the row’s `command` is emitted as `ddflow decision add --id D-{it.id}-Q1 --title <title> --decision <text>`. chunk_findings.detail: The previous confirmed finding 3 is still not fixed in this part: the question source's command changed from `ddflow approvals approve <id>` to `ddflow approvals show <id>`, but `show` is still an approvals read-only command, not the "exact command to answer it" required by the inbox contract, and the source's selector explicitly includes session notes. Given a pending session-note question, the row tells the operator to run `ddflow approvals show <session-note-id>`; session notes are recorded with `ddflow session note <item> --text <answer>`, so the command is in the wrong namespace and will not record an answer. chunk_findings.detail: The replay uses `when = NOW + 1e6` with `NOW` hard-coded to `2026-10-20T10:00:00+00:00`, so `when` is 2026-11-01. But `fold(EventLog(ROOT, log_cfg=Config.load(ROOT).log).read_all(), strict=False)` reads the entire `.ddflow/events` log with no time cutoff. In a checkout whose event log contains records after 2026-11-01 (for example a later proposed decision or a later DECIDE item), `st` includes those future records. The expected counts `open_decides` and `sum(d.status == "proposed" ...)` are computed from that full `st`, while `Q.build(st, Config(), when)` is supposed to be the queue as of `when` and should exclude records newer than `when`. The assertions then spuriously fail even when the queue implementation correctly respects `now`, or they become meaningless if it does not. The replay should cut the folded log at `when` or derive `NOW` from the latest event timestamp.

chunk_findings.detail: These three collectors call `N.make(...)` without passing `command`. For example, `collect_credential` emits a row for an unavailable credential gate with only `default="provide the credential, then re-run the gate (never paste it in chat)"`; `collect_gate_spotcheck` emits only `default="skim the refutations; reopen one you doubt"`; `collect_red_main` emits only `default="have the fix task go first; nothing else should merge meanwhile"`. The operator-inbox contract says every row must contain "the exact command to answer it." With an unavailable-credential gate for item A, the resulting Entry has no actionable command to run, so the operator gets prose but cannot answer the row as required.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/digest/collect_work.py:collect_credential, collect_gate_spotcheck, collect_red_main

chunk_findings.detail: The row's own `detail={"items": items, "gates": lines}` records the items whose refuted passes await spot-check, but `blocks` is explicitly `[]`. Entry semantics in the change state that `blocks` is the list of items (and their transitive dependents) blocked by this human action. chunk_findings.detail: `collect_decide` uses `it.created_at` as the start of the operator's waiting time. But the same function already skips the item while any `needs` are not `DONE`; if a DECIDE doc is created before its prerequisites finish, it became askable only when the last prerequisite completed. Using `created_at` inflates its age and triggers `escalate_after` too early. Example: item `DECIDE-X` created 2026-10-01, need `T` completed 2026-10-30, and `now` is 2026-11-10; the row is aged 40 days instead of 11 days, so severity can escalate after the threshold even though the operator only had 11 days to answer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/digest/collect_work.py:collect_decide:since=it.created_at

chunk_findings.detail: `new = '"6h"'` assigns the TOML string value `"6h"` with literal double-quote characters as part of the value. The intended config value for `digest.escalate_after_red_main` is the duration string `6h`, so the fragment should read `new = "6h"`. Given an existing config that goes through the upgrade fold, the upgrader will record/apply `digest.escalate_after_red_main` as the four-character string `"6h"` instead of `6h`, and later duration parsing of the value will fail or produce a wrong escalation time because the value begins with `"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.digest.escalate_after_red_main.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The replay test is skipped only when `.ddflow/events` does not exist. If that path exists but is empty (a freshly initialized checkout can have an empty `.ddflow/events` file or an empty events directory), `read_all()` returns an empty sequence, `fold` yields an empty `State`, and `when = max(clock.epoch(ev.ts) for ev in events)` raises `ValueError: max() arg is an empty sequence`, failing the test suite instead of skipping or asserting an empty replay.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_digest_queue.py:test_replay_over_the_real_log_is_sane_and_deterministic

chunk_findings.detail: The expected `open_decides` list uses `all(st.items[n].state == DONE for n in i.needs if n in st.items)`. chunk_findings.detail: The command carried by a proposed-decision row is `f"ddflow decision show {d.id}"`. `ddflow decision show` is a display command, not an accept/supersede command; running it leaves the decision with `status == "proposed"`, so the item remains waiting. For example, with decision `D-101` proposed, the row tells the operator to run `ddflow decision show D-101`, then the operator must still know and run another command to accept or supersede it. The row's own default text says "accept it as written, unless you want to change it," but no accepting command is provided, violating the requirement that each row carry the exact command to answer it.

chunk_findings.detail: The required "bugs or completions that need an override the hook forbids to agents" source is unimplemented: `collect_agent_failed` unconditionally returns `[]`. Given a state containing an override-needed completion such as the intent's example `fix-Bci-ruff-check`, no `agent_failed` Entry is produced, so the queue cannot list that item's what/since/command row. The comment that `queue.UNCOLLECTED` names a gap does not provide the required per-item rows, so the folded inbox omits a required class of operator-only work.

chunk_findings.detail: The replay assertion set still never requires `a.entries` to be non-empty, so the prior untriaged finding #6 still holds. In a checkout whose real log has only a non-ask waiting item — for example an unavailable credential gate, a red_main streak, or a finished phase waiting for the lead, with no pending asks, no open DECIDE docs, and no proposed decisions — `E.pending(st, when)` is empty, `open_decides` is empty, and there are no proposed decisions. Then `asked == Counter(...)` is `Counter() == Counter()`, all `all(...)` checks are vacuous, and every assertion passes while `a.entries == ()`.
